steps.what: Check new products, services and price changes for the route
Prepare the relevant customer change notice
Hand the final change notice to the customer
Inform regular customers and answer questions about the changes

tasks.design: Configure a current-change view in {CRM} and a reusable notice layout in {DOCS}. The driver selects and checks relevant changes, hands over the final notice and explains the effect on the customer's purchases.
tasks.previous_blocker: The driver searches several price sheets and rewrites the same change headings.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing account views and document templates may combine approved information.
tasks.still_hard: Customer-specific contracts and objections need explanation.
tasks.human_edge: The driver understands which change matters to this customer.
tasks.altitude: A little less preparation leaves more time for customer questions.

evidence.claim: Native account views and notice templates can remove repeated searching and layout; local time savings are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary includes change lookup, the existing customer notice and its handover and explanation. No routine contact log is invented.

The pricing owner produces product identifier, new price, effective date and account applicability in approved source records. The driver checks them in s1 and selects the notice in s2; retained14 and6 hours include all checking and capture. Missing contract applicability is resolved manually.
Test native views and notice layouts before code. The author saves the notice without a self-approval stage or saving claim for the save itself.
No automatic customer send, pricing decision or new contact record is added.
unknowns: Whether written change notices and account-specific price lists are currently used
research_questions: How much current search and notice layout time can native views remove?

tasks.short: Maintain the daily sales and delivery record

steps.what: Establish actual delivered quantities, returns and sales references
Record sales and delivery information in the daily record
Check the daily record and resolve omissions or quantity differences

tasks.design: Use the native driver form in {OPS_SYSTEM} instead of copying order identifiers and planned lines into a daily paper record. The driver establishes actual quantities, changes planned values where necessary and checks the completed record; its ordinary save is fully retained.
tasks.previous_blocker: Order details are copied again into a daily record before actual quantities are added.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing transport forms can carry order details into the driver's record.
tasks.still_hard: An order quantity is not proof of what was actually delivered or returned.
tasks.human_edge: The driver can reconcile the physical delivery with the customer's account.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive copying leaves more attention for actual discrepancies.

reach.task: Check delivery quantities against order lines

evidence.claim: TransFollow in Qargo supports consignment notes created, issued and signed within the transport system; this supports native delivery-document capability, not the proposed sales saving.
The daily sales-form configuration and retained-time estimate are model knowledge and require local testing.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual-fact collection, daily record writing and checking. Customer payment and receipt creation occur once in3154 and their checked payment reference is reused here.

The order clerk produces order identifier, customer identifier, planned item and unit in existing orders. The driver produces actual delivered and returned quantities in s1 and captures them in s2;35 full observation hours and20 retained writing hours include that work. Unknown quantities and unmatched units require manual entry and checking.
Test the native driver form before custom code. No sensor, signature, discrepancy code or delivery-status flag is assumed to exist without driver capture.
There is no machine commit, automatic customer send or second approval. Ordinary author saving earns no saving; only copying existing order fields is reduced.
unknowns: Current use of paper versus native driver forms
research_questions: Does prepopulating planned fields reduce writing without encouraging false confirmation of actual quantities?

incremental.description: Resolve unmatched order fields and offline form issues

steps.what: Listen to customers' complaints and clarify what happened
Check the delivery facts and permitted remedy
Choose a remedy or escalation within delegated authority
Write the complaint and chosen response in the existing case entry
Explain and agree the response with the customer

tasks.design: Expose the delivery record and current remedy policy together in {OPS_SYSTEM} and use the existing {CRM} complaint form with reusable reference fields. The driver listens, chooses the response, records the real complaint and explains the outcome; no refund or escalation send is automated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Delivery references and remedy instructions are retrieved separately and copied into a complaint form.
tasks.enabler_now: Native links and reference-field reuse can reduce those specific clerical operations.
tasks.still_hard: A disputed delivery or dissatisfied customer requires tact and authority judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The driver repairs trust and recognizes when the issue exceeds delegation.
tasks.altitude: The driver gains a little attention for resolving the issue rather than finding references.

evidence.claim: Native record links and reusable complaint-reference fields can reduce retrieval and copying; no local measured result is available.

assumptions: Boundary includes the actual complaint entry used for follow-up, separately from the conversation. It does not imply a new log for casual questions. Refund execution or a separate escalation message, when needed, is separate work with its own authority and is not automated or counted as removed here.

The customer supplies the account in s1; the driver checks order identifier, disputed line, observed issue and response in s2-s4. Retained12 lookup hours and7 entry hours include capture. Missing references are checked manually.
Test native record links and complaint forms before code. Same-system author saving has no self-approval gate and no saving.
The complaint entry is a case record distinct from the daily sales record in3161.
unknowns: Which complaints currently require a case entry
research_questions: Do native links remove reference copying while preserving accurate complaint descriptions?

tasks.short: Collect payment and issue a customer receipt

steps.what: Collect money from the customer and verify the amount received
Count and give the correct change
Record transactions on customer receipts and check the final details
Give the final receipt to the customer

tasks.design: Use the native receipt form in {OPS_SYSTEM} to reuse order and customer fields instead of handwriting them. The driver still counts money and change, enters actual tender, checks the receipt and physically provides it; no automated payment collection or receipt send is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same customer and order information is handwritten on receipts.
tasks.enabler_now: A native order-linked receipt layout may remove copying and repeated calculations while keeping actual tender entry.
tasks.still_hard: Actual cash received and returned must be checked against reality.
tasks.human_edge: The driver detects short payment and gives clear explanations without delaying the customer unnecessarily.
tasks.altitude: Less receipt copying can shorten a stop; custody of money stays with the driver.

evidence.claim: Order-linked native receipt forms can reduce handwriting of existing transaction details; the time estimate is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes cash collection, change, actual receipt writing and handover. The separate daily record in3161 reuses the payment reference without re-counting this receipt preparation.

The existing order process produces customer identifier, order identifier, amount due and currency. The driver produces actual tender in s1 and change in s2 and captures and verifies them in s3;45 cash-handling hours and22.5 retained receipt hours count all capture and checking. Missing order data uses manual receipt entry.
Test native receipt configuration before custom code. No free payment-status flag is assumed, and a same-system author save has no approval gate or claimed saving.
Any receipt printing already within the form is existing runtime; no new print or electronic send action is proposed.
unknowns: Actual handwriting share and order-linked receipt availability
research_questions: Can reused order fields reduce receipt preparation after tender capture and final checking?
